schema-registry:payments.title: Avro on payments.v1, but no schema registry
schema-registry:payments.message: payments.v1 carries Avro; Payments API writes it and Ledger writer reads it. With no schema registry, consumers can't look up the schema a record was written with, and nothing checks that a new one is compatible.
schema-registry:payments.rationale: Kafka's Avro and Protobuf serializers write a schema id from the registry in front of every record, and the registry refuses a schema change that would break its readers. Without it, producers and consumers have to agree on schemas some other way.

secret-identity:kv.title: 2 services read secrets without an identity
secret-identity:kv.message: Payments API and Ledger writer read secrets from payments-kv, but the diagram doesn't say what they sign in as. With a managed identity, they get in with no stored credential to leak or rotate.
secret-identity:kv.rationale: A service needs a credential to open a vault, and one stored with the service is just one more secret. A workload identity (an Azure managed identity, an AWS IAM role, a Google Cloud service account) signs it in with nothing to store or rotate, and one per service gives each only the access it needs (least privilege).
